credentials.title: Prepare the router and sign in
credentials.description: Copy the script below (click in it, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C), paste it into a RouterOS terminal on the router (WinBox: New Terminal) and run it. It creates a read-only user for Home Assistant, limited to the address {ha_address}, with the one-time password from the Password field, and enables api-ssl. Then press Submit.

data.verify_ssl: Verify the router certificate (needs a CA-signed certificate)

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The router rejected the saved password, or presents a different certificate than before. Home Assistant is now seen as {ha_address}; if that changed, the old user is bound to the old address. Copy the script below, paste it into a RouterOS terminal to reset the user, then press Submit. A changed certificate is trusted only after you have seen its fingerprint and submitted again.

reconfigure.title: Change the router address
reconfigure.description: Use this when the router got another address or the API port changed. The entry keeps its entities; the router must be the same one (same serial number, when it has one).

error.invalid_host: Use an IP address or host name without spaces or quotes.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect. Check the address, port, TLS setting, and that the API service allows this Home Assistant address.
error.invalid_auth: The router rejected the user name or password. If you used the script, check that the router sees Home Assistant at the address named above.
error.certificate_changed: The router presents a different certificate than the one trusted before (SHA-256 {fingerprint}); the password was not sent. If you did not replace the certificate yourself, stop here: another device may be answering on the router's address. Otherwise compare this fingerprint with `/certificate print detail` on the router and press Submit again to trust it.
error.router_error: The router refused a read of the DHCP lease or bridge host tables. The user needs the read and api policies.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.unique_id_mismatch: This is a different router than the one this entry was set up for.

init.title: Choose what to receive
init.description: Everything below is off until you select it. The router pushes the data over the existing connection, so it costs the router next to nothing. Traffic and system values change every few seconds: Home Assistant has no per-entity switch to stop recording them, so add `recorder: exclude: entity_globs:` for them in configuration.yaml if you do not want their history (see the README).

data.track_ports: Ports: link state and negotiated speed
data.track_traffic: Traffic: receive and transmit rate per port
data.track_system: System: CPU, memory, last boot, temperatures, RouterOS update
data.track_uplink: Uplink: the interface of the active default route, i.e. which WAN the router uses
data.update_interval: Seconds between state updates of traffic and system values, and between reads of the uplink
